Perfume rating 3.94 out of 5 with 19,500 votes

Libre by Yves Saint Laurent is a Oriental Fougere fragrance for women. Libre was launched in 2019. Libre was created by Anne Flipo and Carlos Benaïm. Top notes are Lavender, Mandarin Orange, Black Currant and Petitgrain; middle notes are Lavender, Orange Blossom and Jasmine; base notes are Madagascar Vanilla, Musk, Cedar and Ambergris.

Rachael0304 11/15/25 16:23

It’s funny how marketing affects your perception of a scent. My first experience with this scent profile was BBW Fairytail. I found it to be playful and romantic. But when I purchased Libre, I felt like it was a work perfume. This pulls very sweet on me. I pick up nothing sharp even though this scent is dominated by white flowers. The lavender is very strong and reminiscent of a men’s cologne. I love it but not everyone will. This one has a feminine/masculine duality. It can come across as luxury shaving cream, but that is what I love about this. But I do understand why some individuals find that polarizing. So it is not blind buy safe, inspite Libre's popularity. Projection and longevity are both excellent. If you want to try and take the masculine edge off try layering it with Burberry Goddess or Bath and Bodyworks Cloud Nine. This perfume was one of my everyday staples, a 8/10 scent for me. But just as I finished my bottle, Libre Vanilla Couture was released. So I did not repurchase the original and I added the new limited edition to my collection.

anothernose 10/22/25 18:19

I struggle to understand the devotion this fragrance inspires. To me, it smells relentlessly generic — the olfactory equivalent of standing too long at a department store fragrance counter after too many testers.
It projects loudly but says very little. There is a high-gloss, synthetic sheen to it that recalls a dozen other designer launches, all polished, all interchangeable. I keep waiting to find the charm others mention, but it never arrives.
It is not unpleasant, just impersonal — a scent designed for mass appeal that ends up smelling like everyone and no one at once.

This is a great everyday fragrance. I have overlooked it for so long because I’ve been in a love affair with the intense. This summer I found that wearing the intense was too rich. I think this is going to be my everyday and intense for evenings, dates, occasions.

Fell in love the first time I smelled this, so much so that I walked away with a 50ml bottle the very next day. There’s something about Libre that feels like opulence bottle - golden, radiant, and unapologetically bold.

My skin seems to turn its lavender, orange blossom, and vanilla into something deeper, almost sharper, as if it knows exactly how to bend the light of this perfume into another spectrum. It’s proof that skin chemistry is the final perfumer - how the notes hum differently on every body.

Libre is not just feminine or masculine - it’s a fragrance of freedom, suspended between two worlds, commanding attention in either. To wear it is to make a statement: not of gender, but of presence.

Iconic, dramatic, endlessly wearable.

I blind bought Libre because of all those "here's the my biggest compliment getter" tiktoks when I was first starting off with fragrances. Libre improves as it dries down, from a sharp and synthetic opening to an aromatic, white floral musk. Further in the dry down, it lets the warmth of the vanilla note shine without leaning gourmand. The longevity and projection is fabulous, to the point where I'd worry about putting on too much. Libre is good for hot or cold days, and it's bright enough for day time while still having enough edge to it that you could wear it on a night out. With its versatility, I completely get why it's a signature scent for many. I do wish the vanilla and the mandarin stood out more in the perfume. The vanilla only comes out partially, deep into the dry down, and the mandarin is completely absent. I would say this is a safe blind buy if you like aromatic/white floral/musk forward fragrances, but if you want a vanilla and citrus forward perfume, I'd keep looking. Other than that, I'd say that Libre a relatively safe blind buy, even though it's a bit overhyped as a compliment getter. I haven't received compliments with it on, and I hear the same from others.

scentbar 08/09/25 07:06

Libre Eau de Parfum - The Rebel in a Blazer and Heels - If confidence had a scent and strutted down a Parisian boulevard with a lavender latte in one hand and a to-do list in the other, it would smell exactly like Libre. This fragrance is like a power suit in a bottle, tailored, bold, and unapologetically chic.
The opening - Is a zesty burst of mandarin orange and black currant, like a cheeky wink. Then comes the lavender, not your grandma’s sachet, but a cool, modern twist that says, 'Yes, I meditate and run board meetings.
As it settles - Orange blossom and jasmine bloom like a bouquet handed to you by someone who knows you deserve flowers just because. And the base! is like a warm hug of vanilla, musk, and cedar, with a whisper of ambergris that lingers like a compliment you weren’t expecting.
Wear it when - You want to feel like the main character, or when you need a little extra, I’ve got this' energy, smells like a lavender field crashed a fashion show and brought snacks.
The Verdict - Libre is freedom in fragrance, equal parts elegance and edge. Spray it on and let your inner self rock. You want to turn heads, steal hearts, or just feel like the most magnetic version of yourself. Libre it doesn’t whisper—it purrs.

MetaMystic 06/09/25 23:38

I don’t know… to me, this one’s a bit of a chameleon. Every time I try it on, it smells different. I keep wondering, what it depends on: skin chemistry, mood, weather? When it first launched, I thought it was a masculine scent. Now, it feels more unisex. I can’t quite figure out what exactly makes this the best-selling fragrance. It’s definitely pleasant, elegant, with a touch of softness, but not as sharp and edgy as the branding suggests. That said, I do appreciate it.

I’ve seen it compared a lot to Burberry Goddess and Mon Guerlain because of the lavender + vanilla combo. I get the comparison. Guerlain feels the most refined of the three, Burberry is much softer and more feminine, while Libre is somewhat both and neither at the same time.

The dry down is nice, and I could see myself reaching for it now and then, but it’s not something I’d call a signature scent. There’s just not enough definition for me. It smells like a “perfume,” if you know what I mean, not leaning into any one mood or identity. And maybe that’s the point. Maybe that’s exactly why it satisfies so many people, because it’s directionless, in a way that allows it to be anything.

It reminds me of Prada Paradoxe - it's everything, and nothing in particular. Shooting in all directions, which is great for mass appeal, but maybe less so for fragrance lovers who crave something more distinct. WZ05 05/27/25 19:45

YSL Libre series presents itself as a gender-swap scent, aiming to reshape lavender, a note traditionally used mainly in masculine fragrances, into something with a feminine touch. As they put it, it's about "walking the line between the masculine and feminine". There are a lot of promising points there since I personally believe that all perfumes are unisex and I happened to get a sample the EDP version.

Long story short, it's underwhelming, mass-appealing scent at best. It didn't live up to my expectations after a bold manifesto. It's simply fresh floral with a sweet undertone. Pleasant, yes but not nearly revolutionary enough to truly blur the boundaries between floral elegance and aromatic strength. It's ironic that a scent meant to encourage liberation ends up boxing itself as another feminine scent.

Funny enough, this was the first time a fragrance didn't get completely eaten by my skin. The sillage was amazing. Just one spray was enough to assert its existence in an unscented space.

I do adore its dry-down note though. It's musky, warm and easy to be with. This is not a bad scent at all, really. In fact, I can see this be worn by many. It's just unfortunate it didn't reflect its own statement of truly being free as a unisex scent and marketing it as a women scent.

Overall Scent Score: 7/10

My friend brought it over from Europe for my birthday and I though “ oh no , my taste is so particular how could she lol “ however very nice of her . I could always give it away as a gift or wear it on occasion I thought.
I opened it and smelled it and immediately loved it. This stuff is good ! I looked up the notes and was in complete love now. A lavender perfume with vanilla. ...one of my favourite category of all times. This perfume has incredible staying powder , great silage and amazing performance. It’s like a memory of the past , to me it’s Europe in a bottle. This is how perfumes use to perform , memories of the 80s here ,updated. Great quality , elegant , sophisticated yet sexy and warm. It has a sweet creamy vibe which is slightly herbal and aromatic , the vanilla makes it so feminine and sexy , something is slightly fresh it must be the lavender and jasmine and orange musk and ambergris that may appear ever so slightly soapy. All the notes are pretty much a combination of my favourites notes. So to me this perfume is heavenly !
Ambergris , musk , cedar and vanilla are the base of this creamy rich scent that manages to be light and fluffy at the same time. Masterpiece to my nose.

Libre is described as a sexy cool , warm floral walking the line between masculine and feminine ,they say it’s the hottest launch of the year , they say Libres freestyle takes on the fougere , a classic style of men’s fragrances featuring lavender with the warm heart of the vanilla and ambergris and burning hot with orange blossom. ...

The only thing not so great about this perfume is the cheap light plastic cap. It should have more weight to it. It cheapens the perfume bottle somewhat.

I see Sephora carries this now. So I ordered a purse spray from there. Not that it’s needed as this perfume lasts and lasts into the night and next morning.

Wow. I loved this in the store... but I had no idea..

I love it.

DT953 09/06/19 18:06

Look, it's not a bad release or anything and the fact that it's nothing groundbreaking doesn't really take away anything for me ... but it's business perfume, plain and simple. Hitting the right chords to be a big seller and not really building from that. In saying that, it does a good job at that so no complaints.

Once the ultra synthetic opening settles down, it becomes a lovely vanilla and orange blossom fragrance with light herbal aspects that softly waft around you. Would it be someone's signature? Sure, why not. It's a 'live, laugh, love' wall-sign type of scent, though.

msiska 11/10/19 04:52

Oh wow, this is an eye-opener. Libre does smell like free air, but gorgeously fragrant.
The head is so enchanting that I literally gasped. My overall impression is delicate floral. There is no loudness, no cliché. Now and then I get the slightly masculine vibe of lavender, but the whole composition is blended so masterfully that it doesn't feel manly, it just feels confident. Unisex? No way. It is feminine as can be.
And the longevity is exceptional.

puddley 08/29/19 07:34

I was so keen to try this one and it's a whopping disappointment. It's as if someone at YSL decided the following:
1. Fougeres are having a moment
2. Gender neutrality is having a moment
3. La Vie est Belle has been having a moment for years
Lets' combine all three!
The result is that it smells like something your Dad wore in the 80s combined with a bucket of vanilla and ethyl maltol. I didn't think YSL could make a bigger olfactory nightmare than Black Opium but this is a contender.

chicagogirl 11/04/19 15:52

I am a warm, cozy perfume and fruity floral lover so my opinion will probably be affected by this. If you are the opposite of this you'll love it. This has drawn comparisons to Mon Guerlain from a look at the notes, but it is very, very different. MG is a warm, cozy feminine soft perfume. This is an icy, cold, serious, fresh, rugged kind of fragrance IMO. A masculine, fresh, woodsy perfume for women. The masculine notes in this remind me of the masculine notes in CH Good Girl. It's like Good Girl without gourmand notes. Very different perfumes but this has the same slightly masculine tone in the notes. I got a deluxe little sample bottle from Sephora using my points and I am so glad I didn't purchase a full size bottle just from sniffing those little fragrance papers in magazines. In the magazine paper this is a lot warmer, more floral and feminine. But actual perfume is extremely men's cologne-like upon dry down. When first sprayed you get that little bit of vanilla and lavender with extremely fresh, almost pine-y woodsy notes in the background. The fresh woodsy notes totally distinguish this from Mon Guerlain. Within only a few minutes the vanilla is gone and it is just pure woodsy cedar with a distant echo of jasmine. It smells fresh and clean, almost like a men's soap. It has a cologne quality to it.This has the potential to be offensive and disliked in close quarter type jobs in my opinion. It's not soft or subtle at all and very strong. This is coming from someone who almost NEVER says perfumes are too strong (check my reviews lol). I absolutely love, love, love the bottle. It looks regal. YSL makes some of my most beloved perfumes (Mon Paris and Black Opium) but this ain't it sis.

I believe that people enjoy it, but to me, the mix of the powdery lavender, brightness and creamy tone of jasmine with the sweet orange blossom, reminds me of an old sun bleached yellow Tupperware container we use to garden with. Joys of life 08/14/20 16:15

Ok stop lying Yves Saint Laurent, Is there Cashmeran in here?? Or Cashmere woods?

Blergh. This perfume smells like a freshly stocked and mopped dollar store. Add a note of toilet air freshener lavender, and vanilla candles + something ammoniac and boom, you have Libre. (Ok and a lil' orange blossom). I don't hate on fragrances much but this is YSL and.. just.. no.

This is similar to Living Lalique, which shares that lavender/cashmeran/vanilla DNA and is a decent dupe (a bit heavier and more unisex than Libre) at a quarter of the price. Try before you buy.
